workflowRecommendation: One implementer, one PR touching only scripts/smoke/* plus three one-line docs/solutions corrections. Build the relay (task 1) and its bun test first, then up.sh, checkpoints.sh, down.sh, README, and the three shell harnesses. Run the two-rig live proof on this machine before opening the PR. Implement against current main (52c5e03e, which already contains LEGION-10 #957); rebase onto main only when GitHub reports CONFLICTING after #1011 (LEGION-40) or #1010 (LEGION-41) merge - see `rebase` below for the exact hunks that will collide.
prerequisites: `cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && bun install` - the workspace has no root node_modules yet; scripts/smoke/envoy-bridge.ts (and the new relay) import `nats` (^2.29.2, hoisted from packages/daemon) and packages/contracts/src/envelope.ts.

A live Dispatch reachable from this box: DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN exported (pre-LEGION-40) or `~/.config/opencode/envoy.json` `.dispatch.serverUrl`/`.dispatch.token` (post-LEGION-40). Project LEGSMOKE must exist there (it does; every earlier rig used it).

Provider credentials via `secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY GEMINI_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY --` (the generated legion.yaml's default omp_launch_prefix) so the two live rigs' controller and architect panes actually run.

decision.chosen: A sibling relay, `scripts/smoke/issue-relay.ts`, that polls the Dispatch HTTP API for the rig's root issue and its transitive children and publishes each event onto the rig's own NATS as the production outbox would. `scripts/smoke/envoy-bridge.ts` is not modified.
why: The root key does not exist until up.sh's ensure_root_issue runs, and children appear minutes later. A per-rig filter on the upstream core-NATS subscription (`notifications.dispatch.issue.<KEY>.>`) cannot see an event published before it subscribed, so it would need a JetStream consumer on the production ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS stream - coupling the rig to production stream retention, subject permissions and tailnet reachability. `GET /api/v1/issues/<key>/events?after=0` replays the whole history, so ordering relative to root creation stops mattering.

A child's `issue.created` is published on the child's own subject, never under the root's, so child discovery needs the Dispatch API in either design. The filter design would therefore need production NATS *and* the API; the relay needs only the API the rig already requires (DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN are already inputs to up.sh and the daemon).

It removes the production-NATS dependency the LEGION-27 architect asked to remove ('so resync-driven scenarios work without live ingress and without cross-rig contamination'), and it is the mechanism LEGION-27 already proved by hand (/tmp/legion27-smoke-rig/inject-issue-event.ts), made continuous and made exact.
envoy mode stays byte-identical (acceptance 3): no change to envoy-bridge.ts, its test, or the envoy branch of up.sh.
decision.isolationGuarantee:
The relay only ever fetches `/api/v1/issues//events` for keys in its tracked set: the root from SMOKE_ROOT_ISSUE plus the transitive closure of `GET /api/v1/issues?project=

&parent=`. Another rig's root is never a descendant of this root, so its events are never fetched, never published, and the daemon never logs `consumed event` for them. The daemon additionally skips any subject whose key does not start with `-` (events.ts handleEnvelope), and drops a seq not strictly newer than `state.issues[key].lastAppliedSeq` (reducers.ts reduceDispatchEvent), so a relay restart is harmless.

environment.SMOKE_ROOT_ISSUE: required; must match /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$/ (ISSUE_KEY_PATTERN in packages/daemon/src/daemon/legion-state.ts); the project is the prefix before the dash. A wildcard or malformed value is a config error (never widen the subject set).
environment.DISPATCH_TOKEN: required. up.sh passes it in the relay's `env` block exactly as it already does for the daemon (`DISPATCH_TOKEN="$DISPATCH_TOKEN"`); after LEGION-40 the variable is a shell variable assigned by resolve_dispatch_config, not exported, so passing it on purpose is the only way it reaches the child. Never logged.

exports.relayConfigFromEnvironment(env): -> { rootIssue, project, dispatchUrl, token, downstreamUrl }; throws naming the offending variable (mirrors bridgeConfigFromEnvironment).
exports.envelopeForEvent(row): Takes one row of `GET /api/v1/issues/<key>/events` (the Go model.Event: id, issue_key, artifact_id, project, seq, type, actor, notify, created_at, payload) and returns the Envoy envelope exactly as packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/outbox/publisher.go `envelope()` builds it: event_id = `dispatch-<id>`; source = "dispatch"; source_event_id = String(id); source_session = actor.id only when actor.kind === "session"; topic = dispatchIssueSubject(issue_key, type) from packages/contracts/src/subject.ts; dedupe_key = event_id; issued_at = Date.parse(created_at) (ms); payload_summary = `<issue_key> <type with dots replaced by spaces>` plus `: <text>` for ask.* (payload.question, 120 runes), message.created / comment.* / suggestion.* (payload.body), subscription.removed (payload.session_id), whitespace-collapsed and cut at 160 runes (port of payloadSummary; owner is always the issue key - the artifact-slug branch is cosmetic and skipped); payload = JSON.stringify(row) (the same struct the outbox marshals, so the daemon's dispatchIssueEvent decodes it identically); trace_id = event_id. No expires_at, payload_ref, or sender.
exports.messageId(envelope): `${dedupe_key}:${topic}` - what packages/envoy/internal/bus/nats.go sets as nats.MsgId for source "dispatch". Published with `js.publish(topic, data, { msgID })` so the ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS stream's duplicate window (72 h) rejects a replay after a relay restart; the ack's `duplicate` flag is logged.
exports.orderEvents(batches): Concatenates every tracked key's new rows and sorts by `id` ascending (Dispatch allocates event ids in commit order), reproducing the outbox's cross-issue order; within one key this is also ascending seq, which reduceDispatchEvent requires (a lower or equal seq is dropped).
exports.runRelay(config, deps): deps = { fetch, connect, sleep } injectable for the unit test; defaults to globalThis.fetch, nats connect, setTimeout.

loop: Connect downstream once: connect({ servers, name: `legion-smoke-issue-relay-<root>`, reconnect: true, maxReconnectAttempts: -1, reconnectTimeWait: 2000 }); js = nc.jetstream(). No upstream NATS at all.

Every tick (2000 ms constant POLL_INTERVAL_MS; not an env knob): (1) discovery - breadth-first from the root, `GET /api/v1/issues?project=

&parent=` for every tracked key, adding each returned `.key`; log `RELAY TRACKING parent=` once per new key. (2) For every tracked key `GET /api/v1/issues//events?after=&limit=500`, paging until a page is shorter than the limit. (3) orderEvents, then publish sequentially (await each ack) and after each ack set cursor[key] = row.seq; log `RELAYED subject= event= seq= stream_seq= duplicate=`. (4) The first tick whose fetches all succeed logs `RELAY READY root= project=

dispatch= downstream=` exactly once - even with zero events (no events yet: the relay waits; nothing is invented).

Dispatch failure (network error, 5xx, any non-2xx other than 401/403/404-on-root, non-JSON body) or a publish failure: log `RELAY RETRY attempt=<n> next=<ms>ms: <message>`, sleep the backoff (1000 ms doubling to a 30000 ms cap), retry the tick; cursors are only advanced by acked publishes, so nothing is skipped. A later successful tick logs `RELAY RECOVERED after <n> attempts` and resets the backoff. The relay never exits on these.

Definitive misconfiguration - Dispatch answers 401/403 to any request, or 404 for the root issue itself - logs `RELAY UNHEALTHY <message>` and exits 1 (a wrong bearer or a missing root does not heal by waiting; no silent fallback). Config errors from relayConfigFromEnvironment take the same path via the import.meta.main wrapper, as in envoy-bridge.ts.
SIGINT/SIGTERM: stop the loop, drain the connection, exit 0.
relayContract.logMarkers: RELAY READY / RELAYED / RELAY TRACKING / RELAY RETRY / RELAY RECOVERED / RELAY UNHEALTHY - up.sh's wait_for_issue_relay and checkpoints.sh's require_isolated_relay key on these exact prefixes; the README names them.

tasks.title: Write scripts/smoke/issue-relay.ts and scripts/smoke/issue-relay.test.ts
steps: Implement the relay per `relayContract`. Follow envoy-bridge.ts's shape: pure exported config/envelope helpers, `runRelay`, and an `import.meta.main` block that logs `RELAY UNHEALTHY <message>` and sets exitCode 1 on a thrown error.

Unit tests (bun test, same style as envoy-bridge.test.ts): (a) relayConfigFromEnvironment rejects `LEGSMOKE-*`, `LEGSMOKE-1.>`, `legsmoke-1`, and an empty SMOKE_RIG_NATS/DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN, each error naming the variable; derives project `LEGSMOKE` from `LEGSMOKE-7`. (b) envelopeForEvent on the real captured rows packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/fixtures/dispatch/issue-created-root.json, issue-created-child.json and legsmoke-3-issue.updated-human-todo.json: `envelopeValidation(JSON.stringify(envelope))` from ./envoy-bridge is `{valid: true}`; `dispatchIssueEvent(envelope)` from ../../packages/daemon/src/daemon/dispatch-events.ts returns the fixture's key/seq/type and eventId `dispatch-<id>`; event_id === dedupe_key === trace_id; messageId === `dispatch-<id>:notifications.dispatch.issue.<key>.<type>`; source_session is set only for a `kind: "session"` actor. (c) runRelay with a fake fetch/publish/sleep and a tick limit: tick 1 discovers a child from `?parent=`, publishes root then child rows in global id order, records each cursor; tick 2 requests `after=<last seq>` per key and publishes nothing new; a row already published is never published twice. (d) fetch failure on tick 2: a RETRY line, backoff 1000 -> 2000 -> ... capped at 30000, cursors untouched, then a successful tick publishes the missed rows and resets the backoff; 401 throws with the UNHEALTHY message. (e) zero events: READY logged once, nothing published, polling continues.
Run only `bun test scripts/smoke/issue-relay.test.ts` and `bunx biome check scripts/smoke/issue-relay.ts`; do not run the repository suites mid-flight.

Checkpoints 3 and 4 depend on the smoke architect (real OMP + provider credentials via secretsd) posting the spec artifact, opening the design-gate ask (auto-closed, gates.design off) and creating/releasing a child. That is the rig's existing exercise, not new to this change, but it is wall-clock (tens of minutes per rig) and burns provider credit - budget for it.

The relay hands the daemon events in production order, but it polls every 2 s, so a status write the controller makes appears in daemon state up to ~2 s (plus the JetStream round trip) later than under envoy mode. No checkpoint reads state with a deadline tighter than that; keep the constant at 2 s rather than adding an env knob.
rejected: Per-rig filter inside envoy-bridge.ts keyed on the root issue: needs a JetStream consumer on the production ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS stream to see events published before up.sh learns the key (core subscriptions have no history), still needs the Dispatch API to discover children, keeps the production-NATS dependency, and changes the file acceptance 3 says must stay unchanged.

One-shot injection of `issue.created` (the LEGION-27 script as-is, and LEGION-10's Rejected list): every later event - the controller's todo write, ask answers, child creation - would be missing; the relay carries the live feed.

Reading the daemon's `${SMOKE_DIR}/daemon/secrets/dispatch-token` file from the relay instead of passing DISPATCH_TOKEN in its env block: avoids nothing the daemon's own start block does not already do, and couples the rig script to the daemon's private secrets layout.

A persisted relay cursor file: unnecessary - a restart replays from seq 0 and both JetStream (Nats-Msg-Id within the 72 h duplicate window) and the daemon (lastAppliedSeq) discard the replay; the `duplicate=true` acks are the visible proof.

Making `isolated` also start `gh webhook forward` for GitHub events: out of scope (acceptance 2 names checkpoints 1-4 and 12 only) and would reintroduce the user-authenticated gh requirement isolated exists to avoid.
A configurable poll interval / an env knob for the backoff: nothing needs it; constants keep the surface to the four variables above.
nonGoals: No daemon, contracts, or envoy-client change.
No change to envoy or forward behaviour, to envoy-bridge.ts, or to its test.
No new docs/solutions document (retro owns learnings).
